seats.name: seat-1
argv:
Implement format(fmt, ...args) in format.ts according to README.md (keep the export and signature). It must produce exactly the text described there for every format string and argument list the README allows. Use no network or dependencies, and do not shell out to other programs or import a formatting library: the submission is the TypeScript implementation itself. Modify format.ts in this workspace; a chat answer alone is not a submitted implementation. The evaluator runs private tests against your code after completion.

Modify the relevant source file(s) in this shared working directory directly; when the room reaches a proposal you agree with, its text should summarize the fix, but the file edits are the submission.

Join room rq1 as seat-1 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
I implemented `format` in `format.ts`, and room rq1 concluded with all 3 seats agreeing. I've left the room.

I ran the README's rounding examples and a spread of flag, width and precision cases, and the output matched. I also ran a few extreme values and they looked right: `%e` of 5e-324, `%g` of 1.7976931348623157e308, and `%.0f` of 1e21. I haven't compared it against a reference printf, and the private tests haven't been run.

Float rounding for `e`, `f` and `g` uses exact BigInt arithmetic on the binary value, rounding ties to even, as the README requires. Everything else is handled by hand-written parsing: `d i x X o s c` and `%%`, with the flags, width and precision rules from the README.

The proposal's text says "README examples verified by running". The extremes check came after I filed it, so that wording doesn't mention it. The accepted proposal couldn't be amended, so it stays as filed.

seats.text:
`format.ts` now has a full implementation of `format`, and room rq1 concluded with 3 of 3 agreeing. I didn't write the submitted file: another seat had already saved a working one, so I kept theirs after reading it against the README, and my own draft was never saved.

It uses exact BigInt arithmetic to round e/f/g values half-to-even, and handles flags, width and precision for all the conversions the README lists.

I ran spot checks against a copy of it. Every result matched the README:
- **Rounding:** the tie cases (`%.0f` of 0.5, 1.5 and 2.5, and `%.2f` of 0.125 and 2.675).
- **Flags and conversions:** `#` and `0` with `x` and `o`, `g` and `e` output, and `%.3s`.
- **Extreme values:** 5e-324, 1.79e308, 1e21 and 1e22 under `e`, `g` and `f`.

I did not run a complete test suite. The private evaluator tests are the real check.

I've left the room.

seats.text:
The room accepted seat-1's `format.ts` as the submission (proposal `prop_3a2524ee`, 3 of 3 agreed), and I've left the room.

I didn't write the file that ended up in the workspace. My own version was rejected because seat-1 had already saved theirs, so their file is what's in `format.ts`.

I ran a spot check of my own against it. The cases were the README's rounding examples (`%.0f` on 0.5 and 2.5, `%.2f` on 0.125 and 2.675), `%g`, `%#g`, `%#o`, `%010.3f`, `%s` with a precision, and `%G`. All matched the README. I logged the run under `verify/format` on the board.

Subnormal and very large numbers were not run, and neither were other reviewers' checks beyond a spot check. Seat-2 also ran spot tests and found nothing wrong. I read seat-1's rounding code and it looks correct: it uses the exact binary value of the number with ties-to-even.

The private tests haven't run yet, so I can't say how the file scores.
